note: Era 4 (2026-08-31, Q55 ruled): the sensor beam is EDGE-triggered. It fired for any agent STANDING in a live beam, once per beam per tick, while the design it implements is a crossing - an agent who stopped became a permanent siren (614 consecutive ticks measured against ~56 for a real crossing). beam.inside records who was tripping it last tick, meaning inside AND LIVE, so an agent who waits out the dark window and is still there when the beam returns is still tripped - otherwise 'wait for the gap' becomes 'stand in the gap forever'. Measured effect: beamTripped 1687 -> 36 across four seeds, a 47x reduction in wire and client noise. IMPORTANT AND HONEST: this did NOT fix the 36% of worlds that never reach tier 3, which is what it was built to fix. raiseAlarm is idempotent while an alarm is already live, so the repeat trips were never causing the escalation - alarmEscalated stayed at 144 and every outcome was byte-identical. The real driver is 'sustained' escalation (144 vs 18) and 'burned' raises (97 vs 25); beam-reason alarms are 8 vs 0. The beam change is kept because it is correct on its own terms, not because it solved the spiral. New hashed state (beam.inside) in both twins, copied deeply in copyState and mirrorState - a spread alone would share the array by reference.
